images.caption: Front of the Eleutheros Cooke House, located at 1415 Columbus Avenue in Sandusky, Ohio, United States.  Built in 1844 and moved to this spot in 1874, it is listed on the National Register of Historic

brief: An island-town cottage lot: Eleutheros Cooke House at 1415 Columbus, a 19th-century Lake Erie house; see the photo for its massing, porch and trim. One photo; year estimated. Older than 1970: the Lake Erie shore towns that stand in for Victory Bay's island streets (Vermilion, Sandusky, Put-in-Bay) were built 1840-1920, and Commons has almost no newer cottages there. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Eleutheros Cooke House (Sandusky, 1844): a cut-limestone castellated (crenellated parapet) house, five bays with attic windows, a crenellated entry porch, side wing; now a house museum and garden with a sign

why.note: Sandusky sits on Columbus limestone, quarried in town: its 19th-century houses are grey limestone
